blocks.field3: Some Albion matches belong to the history even when they do not belong to the official league totals.
blocks.field6: Albion began the 1939/40 Second Division campaign with a win at Swansea Town, a draw at Coventry and a 4–3 home defeat to Tottenham. Britain declared war on Germany the day after the Spurs match. League football was suspended and the season was annulled.
blocks.field7: These three games were played, but their results were erased from the league record. They appear here as historical records, outside the competitive ledger and the rivalry totals. Scores below put Albion first; Swansea Town retains its name at the time.

blocks.field3: Shared streets, divided households and afternoons remembered for decades. These four neighbouring clubs have their own place in Albion’s history.
Explore the included meetings in the ledger.
blocks.field5: A rivalry written across the Black Country.
blocks.field6: The fixture reaches back beyond the Football League. Wolves’ own history records a Birmingham Senior Cup meeting in January 1883, while Albion’s national cup record begins with the clubs’ FA Cup encounters later that decade. Those different competition boundaries are one reason historical head-to-head totals can vary.
blocks.field7: The rivalry has also been a race played out over months. In 2002, Albion reeled in Wolves to secure automatic promotion. Five years later, the clubs met in a Championship play-off semi-final, Albion winning both legs before losing the final to Derby County.
blocks.field8: Some matches refuse to fade: the 3–0 FA Cup win at Molineux in 2007; the 5–1 league victory there in 2012; the meeting at The Hawthorns in January 2024, won 2–0 by Wolves. The ledger lets you place each afternoon among all the less celebrated meetings around it.

blocks.field3: Explore the included meetings in the ledger.
blocks.field5: Three finals before the century turned.
blocks.field6: Albion and Villa contested the FA Cup final three times in nine seasons. Villa won in 1887, Albion answered with a 3–0 victory in 1892, and Villa took the 1895 final 1–0. These were neighbours meeting on the biggest stage English club football had.
blocks.field7: Both were founder members of the Football League. Their story runs through the beginnings of organised league football as well as cup glory, long before modern divisions and television schedules changed how often they met.
blocks.field8: In 2019, another promotion place lay beyond the derby. Villa won the first play-off leg 2–1; Albion won the return 1–0 after extra time. Villa advanced on penalties. The distinction matters: a match can belong to Albion while the tie belongs to the opposition.

blocks.field6: The Wembley afternoon that made a double.
blocks.field7: Albion’s 1931 FA Cup final put two neighbouring clubs opposite one another at Wembley. W. G. Richardson scored both goals in a 2–1 win over Birmingham. Albion then secured promotion, completing a combination of achievements that still defines the season.
blocks.field8: The road to Wembley brought them together again in 1968, this time in a semi-final at Villa Park. Albion won 2–0 and went on to lift the cup against Everton. In this local history, the grounds of one neighbour can become the setting for another neighbour’s story.
blocks.field9: League meetings add a different rhythm: familiar journeys, changing fortunes and a result that matters well beyond one afternoon. The archive includes the latest league meeting checked for this edition, Albion’s 0–1 home defeat on 10 October 2026.

blocks.field3: Explore the included meetings in the ledger.
blocks.field5: A local story with a different rhythm.
blocks.field6: Walsall belongs in the map of Albion’s neighbours, even though meetings in the national competitions have been less frequent than those with Wolves or Villa. It is a different relationship, shaped by the occasions when their paths cross.
blocks.field7: One meeting began a trophy-winning journey. Albion’s first League Cup match was a 3–1 victory over Walsall on 22 September 1965. By the following March, the Baggies had beaten West Ham over two legs to lift the cup.
blocks.field8: That makes the Walsall result more than an opening-round score: it is the first step in one of the museum’s silverware stories. Local and regional cup fixtures and friendlies are outside this ledger, so its meeting count is deliberately limited to the competitions included.

blocks.field2: A derby once ended with a shared Shield.
blocks.field3: Albion and Wolves drew 4–4 at Molineux in the 1954 Charity Shield. The trophy was shared. Not every local meeting ends with just one set of happy supporters.
